newsitem.title: UK: Halifax drops to lowest since flotation.
newsitem.headline: Halifax drops to lowest since flotation.

text.p: Halifax Plc shares fell to their lowest level since last month's flotation on Monday as some investors cashed in gains ahead of the reporting season for banks, kicked off on Tuesday by Abbey National Plc, dealers said.

Halifax shares were down 11-1/2p to 709 by 0954 GMT in volume of 3.5 million shares, below their close of 734-1/2p on their first day of trade on June 2. It hit a post-flotation high of 784p on June 20.
Abbey was up 1-1/2p at 820-1/2, after earlier slipping into negative territory.
Dealers said Abbey's results could bear the scars of continued competition among mortgage lenders, emphasising Halifax's continued high stock market valuation.
"There are still plenty of people out there offering to lend us money to buy cars and houses," said one senior dealer.

"But if Halifax dropped back to say around the 650p level one would have to look very closely at this stock...there is no doubt the company is well positioned to participate in the restructuring of the financial sector."

Abbey's results are expected to show first-half pre-tax profit rising more than 20 percent to at least 675 million stg, though that figure will be flattered by the acquisition of National & Provincial Building Society and underlying growth is expected to be modest.
